title: Proactive soft-degrade regional SLO harmonizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multi-region routing today uses hard thresholds for geo-pinning and capacity-based shedding. During transient spikes this causes oscillation (flip-flopping pins, repeated circuit-breaker tripping) that increases tail latency and customer errors.

Goal: Implement a runtime 'SLO harmonizer' agent that smooths decisions across regions by maintaining short-lived regional SLO estimates, applying hysteresis and a credit-based soft-degrade mechanism. The agent should: (1) reduce oscillation in pin/evict decisions, (2) allow graceful degradation via soft eviction credits before hard shedding, (3) coordinate with circuit breakers and autoscaler hints, and (4) expose observability for rollout evaluation.

Deliverables:
- SLO estimator: rolling quantile/median windows per-region and per-model-route.
- Hysteresis policy: configurable growth/decay windows to avoid thrash.
- Eviction credits ledger: tokens granted when region performs below SLO, spent to evict lower-priority traffic; credits decay if region recovers.
- Circuit breaker tie-in: CRB enters soft-tripped state before full-open; soft-tripped triggers credit spending rather than immediate failover.
- Routing API flags: ability to prefer latency-floor preserved traffic (pin set) and to mark classes that can be softly degraded (background, low-QoS).
- Telemetry: new metrics (harmonizer_decisions_total, credit_balance, slo_estimate_{p50,p95}, harmonizer_oscillation_rate) and dashboards.

Non-goals: Replacing existing steering matrix or global routing algorithms. This is a coordinated layer intended to reduce short-lived churn and enable smoother multi-region failovers.
